priorPlan.intro: Day 1: Zion Canyon Visitor Center; Pa'rus - Diversion Dam; Lunch and a shaded break; Human History Museum. Day 2: Lower Emerald Pool Trail; Upper Emerald Pools Trail; Lunch and recovery break; Canyon Junction. Day 3: Riverside Walk; The Narrows; Dry off, eat, and rest. Day 4: West Rim to Scout Lookout; Lunch and a long recovery break; Canyon Junction.

days.label: Pa’rus scenery and Zion’s human stories

stops.name: Zion Canyon Visitor Center
stops.note: Start with the outdoor exhibits and ask about current trail access and transportation for your four days.

stops.name: Pa'rus - Diversion Dam
stops.note: Make this an unhurried walking and photography outing, with time to enjoy the canyon rather than treating the dam as a quick checkpoint. Bring drinking water and sun protection.
stops.why: An easier first outing gives you time to settle into Zion before the longer hikes.

stops.name: Lunch and a shaded break
stops.note: Bring lunch and take a proper break before the afternoon visit.

stops.name: Human History Museum
stops.note: Explore the human-history exhibits and the 22-minute orientation film, then spend time enjoying the mountain views outside. Confirm museum hours for your dates.
stops.why: The stories and exhibits add something different after a morning spent looking at the landscape.

days.label: Emerald Pools and a canyon-view finish

stops.name: Lower Emerald Pool Trail
stops.note: Begin your Emerald Pools outing here. Before setting out, confirm the accessible trailhead and which connecting paths are open; the pool trails should not be treated as guaranteed through-routes.

stops.name: Upper Emerald Pools Trail
stops.note: Continue to the upper pool using the open, signed route. Allow time for uneven footing, a pause at the pool, and the walk back to your starting point; this block includes the return portion of the outing.
stops.why: Making the pools one sustained outing gives the day a substantial hike without adding another distant trail.

stops.name: Lunch and recovery break
stops.note: Eat your packed lunch after the hike and leave time to rest before moving on.

stops.name: Canyon Junction
stops.note: Finish with canyon views and photography from a permitted pedestrian area. Confirm how to reach it that day, and do not stop in the roadway or assume parking will be available.

stops.name: Riverside Walk
stops.note: Use this as the walking approach to your river outing, taking time to enjoy the narrowing canyon. This time allowance covers the Riverside Walk portions before and after The Narrows.

stops.name: The Narrows
stops.note: Plan a bottom-up, out-and-back river hike with a conservative turnaround rather than a distance goal. Before entering, confirm NPS access, flow, flash-flood guidance, and water temperature, and arrange suitable footwear and equipment. Do not enter if conditions are unsafe. NPS warns against drinking river water or submerging your head.
stops.why: This is the day's main experience, so there is no separate afternoon hike competing for your energy.

requirements.title: Permit required
requirements.plannerRule: The Narrows requires a permit. If you include it, state the permit requirement in the same breath.

stops.name: Dry off, eat, and rest
stops.note: Keep dry clothing and food for after the outing. Leave the remainder of the day easy rather than committing to another timed visit.

days.label: Scout Lookout and a quiet canyon finish

stops.name: West Rim to Scout Lookout
stops.note: Give this strenuous uphill outing most of the morning, including breaks and the descent. Bring food, ample water, and sun protection, and confirm trail conditions before starting. Scout Lookout is your turnaround; this plan does not include the Angels Landing extension.
stops.why: A substantial elevated-view hike makes the final day different from the riverside and pool outings.

stops.name: Lunch and a long recovery break
stops.note: Take the afternoon slowly after the climb, with time to eat and rest before a final scenic stop.

stops.name: Canyon Junction
stops.note: Revisit for a relaxed final look at the canyon and late-afternoon photographs. Use permitted pedestrian areas and the access arrangements checked earlier in the trip.
stops.why: A familiar scenic stop is a gentler finish than adding another hike after Scout Lookout.

narrativeSections.heading: Why this trip works
narrativeSections.markdown: The 4 days are grouped so nearby sights in Zion National Park work together instead of bouncing across the park.
